- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently overpredicts in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — apply downward bias early.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overreacts and forecasts continued rise — cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or apply mean reversion.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.5 within 3 days), model fails to adjust quickly — reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is high but price history shows strong upward momentum — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.7 and recent price > previous 5-day high.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for days 25–30 if sentiment remains positive or shows no reversal.
